newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV REBOUNDS AT CLOSE ON CEN.BANK SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV REBOUNDS AT CLOSE ON CEN.BANK SUPPORT.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev rebounded to 274-276 per dollar at close from 277-284 afternoon lows after joint support from the central bank and other banks but was still down from 273 in the morning, dealers said.
"The central bank stepped up (foreign currency) sales after the lev slumped to new record lows and a couple of state banks joined it later on, boosting the lev," a commercial bank dealer said.
The trader declined to name the commercial banks.
The central bank (BNB) sold dollars at exchange rates from 279 levs in the early afternoon to around 274 at the close of the interbank trade, dealers said.

"Dollar offers between 277-284 levs per dollar that some banks quoted in the early afternoon were deemed unrealistically high by buyers and BNB sales of small volumes at lower rates propped up the lev," another dealer said.
Central bank officials were not available for comment.

The lev's fall from around 270 per dollar at the prevoius close of the interbank market was triggered mainly by a dollar rush on the cash market due to uncertainty over potential implications of a currency board system proposed for Bulgaria.
The lev fell to 290 on the cash market in the afternoon from 275 in the morning.

The head of the State Savings Bank, Bistra Dimitrova, told parliament on Friday two billion levs had been withdrawn from her bank since Monday and some clients were asking the bank to buy back their Treasury paper ahead of maturity because they feared it would not be redeemed in cash.
Pegging the lev to a major currency through a currency board system was proposed last week by the International Monetary Fund to help defeat hyperinflation and restore confidence in the battered lev.
Under the scheme the amount of levs in circulation must be exactly matched by the amount of the country's foreign exchange reserves. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
